paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: when trouble comes, take it to the LORD. Israel got hit by the king of Arad, and some of them were taken prisoner. They didn't panic and they didn't stew. They made a vow to the LORD and asked for His help (Numbers 21:1-2).

Now look at who they asked. They said, "If You will deliver this people into our hands…" (Numbers 21:2). That's not a sneaky side deal. That's a people saying the win has to come from Him. Then the text says, "the LORD heard Israel's plea and delivered up the Canaanites" (Numbers 21:3). He heard them, friend. HEARD them.

And then Israel kept the vow. Making a promise when you're in a tight spot is easy, but remembering it once the trouble is gone is the hard part (Numbers 21:3). So here's my question for you, baker: what have you said to the LORD that you haven't gotten around to doing yet? I've left plenty of things half-done on my own counter, so I'm not throwing stones. Bring your trouble to Him, trust Him to hear you, and then do what you said you'd do.
